meta.title: Data, paths and networking | ProxMenux
meta.description: How OCI manager Apps keeps the data of an OCI container: container disks, host directories, Rclone mounts, addresses and private networks.

header.title: Data, paths and networking
header.description: What lives in the rootfs, what survives its replacement, how data is shared between containers and how each container gets its address.

calloutInfo.title: Persistence is decided before the LXC exists
calloutInfo.body: The volumes published by the image and by its Compose file are read before the container is created. Every path that has to survive an update becomes a mount point independent of the rootfs, so the rootfs only holds what belongs to the image and can be replaced.

sections.title: What the installer asks
sections.intro: The template supplies the paths the application needs. Each one is placed on a container disk or on a host directory, and more paths can be added before the summary.

items.title: Required paths
items.body: /config, /data, libraries, downloads and every volume the application declares are listed.

items.title: Location
items.body: Each path is placed on a disk of the container or on an existing host directory.

items.title: Storage and size
items.body: A container disk is created on a Proxmox VE storage, local-lvm by default, with the size given. It appears as vm-VMID-disk-N and is attached as mpN.

items.title: Host directory
items.body: A host directory is given by its path. A directory that does not exist is created, owned by the user the container maps.

items.title: Additional paths
items.body: More pairs of host path or volume and container path can be added before installing.

items.title: Summary
items.body: The complete mapping is shown before the CT is created and is stored in its instance contract.

blocks.p: The rootfs is reserved for the binaries and the content of the image. An update or a recreation replaces it without touching either kind of mount point.

sections.title: Example: a container with both locations

code.title: Jellyfin installed as CT 151 on local-lvm (excerpt)
code.code:
rootfs: local-lvm:vm-151-disk-0,size=8G
# Container disk, part of the CT backup
mp0: local-lvm:vm-151-disk-1,mp=/config,backup=1,size=16G

# Host directory, outside the CT backup
mp1: /mnt/oci-shared/media,mp=/data/media

blocks.p: An update or a recreation replaces only the rootfs: mp0 keeps users, libraries and settings, and mp1 keeps showing the same media. Restoring the CT backup brings back /config; the media directory is restored, if needed, from the backup of the host storage.

flow.caption: The application sees the path the image publishes; only where it is stored changes.

blocks.p: Each container keeps its configuration on its own disk. The library or the downloads are one host directory mounted at the same internal path in every container, so a path that one application writes is the same path another one reads.

sections.title: Cloud storage through the Rclone application
sections.intro: The Rclone application of the catalog offers, besides its installation, Enable a mount on an existing Rclone OCI container. It mounts a remote already created and authorised in the Rclone web UI and publishes it on the host, where other containers can use it as a host directory.

items.title: Container and remote
items.body: The VMID of the Rclone container, the exact name of the remote and, optionally, a path inside it.

items.title: Mount name and cache
items.body: The name of the mount and the VFS cache mode: off, minimal, writes or full (default).

items.title: Published views
items.body: A common root, /mnt/oci-shared by default, holds a read/write view in /mnt/oci-shared/remotes/NAME and a read-only view in /mnt/oci-shared/remotes-ro/NAME.

items.title: Activation
items.body: After a confirmation, the CT is stopped, its start command and a Proxmox VE hookscript are set, and it is started again. The operation waits until both views are mounted on the host.

calloutInfo.title: If the mount does not come up
calloutInfo.body: The previous configuration of the container is restored and it is started again, so a failed activation leaves Rclone as it was.

sections.title: Addresses and networks
sections.intro: A single application needs an address. A multi-container application also needs a stable network between its members.

items.title: Single application
items.body: Bridge and DHCP or a fixed CIDR address are chosen. The LXC has an address of its own and the summary shows the complete URLs of the services.

items.title: Multi-container application
items.body: A free subnet is found, a persistent private bridge is created and each member (application, database, cache) gets a fixed address on it.

flow.caption: Dependencies talk over the private network and have no address on the LAN.

blocks.p: The stack contract stores bridge, subnet, addresses and the relations between services. Updating or recreating a member reuses the same topology. ProxMenux Monitor opens the main container at its LAN address, not at its address on the private network.

items: New directories are created with the UID and GID the unprivileged LXC maps.
Existing directories are not re-owned recursively.
Sockets, system files and sensitive paths are not offered as generic host directories.
